# Receipts of thought

> A receipt of thought is a signed, tamper-evident record of how a piece of writing was actually made: the composition timeline, the passages an author discloses as AI-written, the claims they sourced and an embedded content credential. Anyone can verify one in a browser at receiptsofthought.com, with no server involved. The format and its verifier are open source under Apache-2.0.

When text is cheap to generate, a clean final draft is no longer evidence that someone thought. What stays scarce is the record of the work itself. A receipt makes that record verifiable: tampering after signing is detectable, and the check runs entirely client-side so nothing you drop leaves your machine.

## What a valid receipt proves

- Nothing in the receipt was altered after it was signed: the title, the text, the composition timeline, the disclosed AI passages and the sourced claims.
- The composition timeline is exactly the one that was signed: no checkpoint has been reordered, inserted or removed since.
- The embedded C2PA-aligned content credential carries its own valid signature and binds the same text and the same key as the receipt around it.

## What it does not prove

- Who holds the signing key. A key belongs to a machine and its owner, not to a verified identity.
- That the timeline reflects honest work. The signature binds the timeline that was presented at signing, so an author could compose elsewhere, or prune the record, and sign the tidy version.
- That undisclosed text is human-written. Disclosure is the author's choice; the receipt binds what was disclosed, not what was not.

## How to verify one

Open [receiptsofthought.com](https://receiptsofthought.com/) and drop the `.receipts.json` file on the page. The check runs in the browser with WebCrypto: the file is never uploaded, and the page makes no network request while verifying, which its content security policy enforces. A verifier can also be built from the specification alone, and this one can be self-hosted.

## The pieces

- The verifier: [receiptsofthought.com](https://receiptsofthought.com/) checks a `.receipts.json` bundle in the browser.
- The format and verifier source: the open Apache-2.0 trust core, including the receipts format specification, the Ed25519 signing scheme and the client-side verifier.
- Folio: the desktop writing app for macOS and Linux that produces receipts as you write. Folio itself is proprietary; the format and verifier it produces receipts for are not, which is why a receipt can be checked without it.

## Who makes it

Ad Astra Computing. The receipts format and verifier are open so anyone can read, reimplement or host the verification.
